doc: The saved form of a [CanvasElement]: screen-space UI drawn over the game, with sizes and offsets in dp.

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: What the element is.

fields.name: anchor
fields.doc: Screen point the element is placed from.

fields.name: offsetX
fields.doc: Horizontal offset from the anchor.

fields.name: offsetY
fields.doc: Vertical offset from the anchor.

fields.name: width
fields.doc: Width. Not negative.

fields.name: height
fields.doc: Height. Not negative.

fields.name: text
fields.doc: A `Text` element's content, or a `Button`'s label.

fields.name: fontSize
fields.doc: Text size. Above 0.

fields.name: color
fields.doc: Foreground color, `#RRGGBB` or `#RRGGBBAA`.

fields.name: background
fields.doc: Background color, `#RRGGBB` or `#RRGGBBAA`.

fields.name: value
fields.doc: A `Bar`'s fill, from 0 to 1.

fields.name: order
fields.doc: Draw order. Lowest draws first.

fields.name: visible
fields.doc: Whether the element is drawn.

fields.name: action
fields.doc: Name of what the element does for the game, such as `jump`. The game decides what each name means. In a played project, an element naming one of the scene's [input actions](#input_actions) adds to it, and its presses are used up: a Joystick steers an axis such as `move`, and a Button holds and presses a button such as `jump` or `run`. Any other name is left for the game to read.

fields.name: doubleAction
fields.doc: What a Button does when double-clicked: two presses within half a second. The second press also fires `action`. Like `action`, a name among the scene's input actions is pressed, and any other is left for the game to read with `consumeDoublePress()`.

fields.name: touchOnly
fields.doc: Draw only where touch controls are shown.

fields.name: style
fields.doc: How the element looks beyond its colours, as an AwakeKt Compose `Style`: `background`, `gradient` (`start`, `end`, `horizontal`), `image`, `fillImage`, `fillImageMode`, `cornerRadius`, `borderWidth`, `borderColor`, `shadow` (`color`, `offsetX`, `offsetY`, `blur`, `spread`), `textColor`, `textShadow` (`color`, `offsetX`, `offsetY`), `textOutline` (`color`, `width`), `alpha`, and `hovered` and `pressed` states for a Button. `image` is an `Image`'s picture, a frame, or a `Bar`'s track; `fillImage` is a `Bar`'s fill, cut at `value` or, with `fillImageMode` `Squeeze`, drawn at the filled width with both end caps kept. Each image is a `CanvasImage`: `path`, a region (`regionX`, `regionY`, `regionWidth`, `regionHeight`), slice insets (`sliceLeft`, `sliceTop`, `sliceRight`, `sliceBottom`), `repeatEdges`, `repeatCenter`, `tint` and `pixelated`. See [Game UI](../guides/game-ui.md#style-an-element).

fields.name: textAlign
fields.doc: Where a `Text`'s or `Button`'s text sits in the element. None keeps the kind's own: top-left for a `Text`, centred for a `Button`.

fields.name: follow
fields.doc: The name of a node the element follows on screen. Its `anchor` point stands on the node's projected position, nudged inward by its offsets, and it hides when the node is behind the camera or missing.

fields.name: followOffset
fields.doc: World-space offset from the followed node, such as above its head.

fields.name: followBounds
fields.doc: Cover the screen rectangle of the followed node's meshes instead of standing at its point. Its children anchor to that box's edges.

fields.name: followOutset
fields.doc: With `followBounds`, how far the box reaches past the node's rectangle on each side, in dp, so corner children sit outside the node. Negative pulls it in, never below nothing.

fields.name: layout
fields.doc: Lay the element's children out in rows or columns instead of anchoring each: `direction` (`Row` · `RowReverse` · `Column` · `ColumnReverse`), `wrap`, `gap`, `padding`, `justify` (`Start` · `Center` · `End` · `SpaceBetween` · `SpaceAround` · `SpaceEvenly`) and `align` (`Start` · `Center` · `End` · `Stretch`). A laid-out child keeps its `width` and `height` and ignores its anchor and offsets. See [Game UI](../guides/game-ui.md#lay-out-children).

fields.name: grow
fields.doc: In a parent with a `layout`, this element's share of its line's leftover space. Not negative.

fields.name: bind
fields.doc: Game state the element shows without code. `node` names a node; `value` is a `component.field` for a Bar's fill, divided by `max` (a field or a number); `text` fills each `{component.field}`, or `{component.field:n0}` with a number format, in a Text's or Button's words. See [Game UI](../guides/game-ui.md#show-game-state).
